short: Peru has an AI law, Ley No. 31814 of 2023, and a Regulation (Supreme Decree No. 115-2025-PCM) that adds risk tiers, prohibited uses and phased obligations, but sets no sanctions of its own.
title: Peru AI Laws
subtitle: Law No. 31814 and its 2025 Regulation: risk tiers and prohibited uses, without a sanctions catalogue
body_html:
Status at a glance

AI law in force, without penalties. Peru's Ley No. 31814, which promotes the use of AI for economic and social development, was published in El Peruano on 5 July 2023. Its Regulation, approved by Supreme Decree No. 115-2025-PCM, dated 8 September 2025 and published the next day, gives it substance: risk tiers, a list of prohibited uses, transparency and human oversight duties, and impact assessments, phased in by sector over one to four years. It sets no sanctions of its own. Verified on 25 October 2026 against El Peruano and the Congress's consolidated text.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPublishedIn force and phased dates
Law promoting the use of artificial intelligenceLey No. 31814El Peruano, 5 July 2023
Regulation of Law No. 31814Decreto Supremo No. 115-2025-PCMDated 8 September 2025; published 9 September 202590 working days after publication. Public sector: executive, legislature, judiciary and constitutional bodies within one year; regional governments and public universities two years; local governments three years. Private sector: health, education, justice, security, economy and finance one year; transport, commerce and labour two; production, agriculture, energy and mining three; all other uses four. Small firms two years, micro firms three (First Complementary Final Provision).
National AI Strategy 2026 to 2030Resolución Ministerial No. 152-2026-PCMReported by El Peruano, 1 May 2026Policy

Who regulates and enforces

  • Presidency of the Council of Ministers, Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (SGTD): the technical and normative authority (Law art. 4; Regulation arts. 8 and 9.1), with monitoring by its Under-Secretariat for Digital Technologies and Security (art. 35).
  • National Authority for Personal Data Protection: data protection breaches under Ley No. 29733 (Regulation art. 26.2) and complaints (art. 36.2).

Scope and reach

The Regulation applies to public entities, state enterprises, and the private sector, civil society, citizens and academia within the national digital transformation system (art. 3). It excludes personal use, and defence and national security unless they meet the principles of article 7 (art. 4). No extraterritorial trigger was found.

Core obligations

  • Prohibited uses (art. 23.1): manipulation, lethal autonomy without human oversight in civilian contexts, mass surveillance without legal basis, inferring sensitive data from biometrics, real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces (with exceptions), and crime prediction from profiling.
  • High-risk uses (art. 24): critical infrastructure, assessment of minors in education, hiring, social programmes, credit scoring and access to health care.
  • Algorithmic transparency and explanation (art. 25); human oversight (arts. 28.11 and 31.4).
  • Impact assessments: mandatory and documented for public entities (art. 30); voluntary for the private sector, with records kept at least three years (art. 32).
  • Public bodies adopt an institutional AI policy and the national standard NTP-ISO/IEC 42001:2025 (arts. 28.1 and 28.2).

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Non-compliance by public officialsNo sanction set in the Regulation; referred to the Comptroller General of the RepublicRegulation art. 34.1SGTD; Contraloría General
Personal data breachesThe sanctions regime of the personal data protection lawRegulation art. 26.2; Ley No. 29733National Authority for Personal Data Protection

What is coming next

  • The first tranche of obligations, one year into the phase-in, for national government bodies and for private-sector AI in health, education, justice, security, and economy and finance. The point from which the periods run is not stated plainly in the text.

Related

  • AI lawsuit tracker and AI news

Sources

  • Ley No. 31814, El Peruano

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: the exact in-force date of the Regulation, which depends on how working days are counted, and the maximum fines of Ley No. 29733, whose official copy is a scanned image.
